lines.text: Unemployed.
You are entitled to an unemployment benefit [WW-uitkering] if you are unemployed.
That is possible if you have been in salaried employment for more than half a year and you were dismissed [ontslagen] — so not if you resigned [ontslag] yourself.
Problems with your health.
If you become ill, you are entitled to your salary.
Do you have no employer (for example with a temp agency)?
Then you can come under the Sickness Benefits Act [ziektewet].

You can get a disability benefit [WIA-uitkering] if you are unfit for work [arbeidsongeschikt]: you can no longer work because of your health (physical [lichamelijk], or mental [psychisch]) and you have been unable to work for more than two years.
If you need a benefit.
Are you dismissed or do you become unfit for work?
Then contact the UWV immediately: an organisation that helps when you are looking for work.
You must first register there; they help you find a job and apply for a benefit.
You can apply for a benefit one week before you become unemployed.
You have no right to a benefit if you resign yourself.
Social assistance.
Are you not entitled to any other benefit?
Then you can sometimes apply for social assistance [bijstand].
The municipality [gemeente] assesses whether you are entitled to it.
You only get bijstand if you do not have enough money to live on — not if your partner earns enough.
People with savings [spaargeld] must use that up first.
Bijstand is not much money.
Taking a course while on a benefit.
Do you want to take a course or study programme?
Then always consult [overleg] with the UWV or the municipality.
They check whether your chances of finding work will improve and whether you remain available for work.
Sometimes it is mandatory [verplicht] to take courses while on a benefit, for example to learn how to apply for jobs.
Duties while on a benefit.
Do you have WW or bijstand?
Then you must make an effort to find work.
In principle you must accept [accepteren] a job that is offered.
Your benefit is reduced if you find a part-time job, and stops if your income is high enough.
You must report [doorgeven] it if your situation changes, for example if you start to live together [samenwonen].
If you register with the KvK, your benefit in principle stops.
